items.name: Baden-Württemberg
items.blurb: Baden-Württemberg, commonly shortened to BW or BaWü, is a landlocked state in Southwest Germany, east of the Rhine, which forms the southern part of the country's western border with France.

items.name: Bavaria
items.blurb: Bavaria, officially the Free State of Bavaria, is a landlocked state of Germany. It borders the states of Baden-Württemberg to the west, Hesse to the north-west, and Thuringia and Saxony to the north, as well as the countries of Switzerland and Austria to the south and the Czech Republic to the east.

items.name: Berlin
items.blurb: Berlin is the capital and largest city of Germany. With 3.7 million inhabitants, it has the highest population within its city limits of any city in the European Union.

items.name: Brandenburg
items.blurb: Brandenburg, officially the State of Brandenburg, is a landlocked state in northeastern Germany. Brandenburg borders Poland and the states of Berlin, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Lower Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt, and Saxony.

items.name: Bremen
items.blurb: Bremen, officially the Free Hanseatic City of Bremen, is the smallest and least populous of Germany's 16 states. It is informally called Land Bremen, although the term is sometimes used in official contexts.

items.name: Hamburg
alt: Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg
items.blurb: Hamburg, officially the Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg, is the second-largest city in Germany after Berlin and sixth-largest city in the European Union, with a population of over 1.9 million.

items.name: Hesse
items.blurb: Hesse or Hessen, officially the State of Hesse, is a landlocked state in Germany. Its capital city is Wiesbaden, and the largest urban area is Frankfurt am Main, which is also the country's principal financial centre.

items.name: Lower Saxony
items.blurb: Lower Saxony is a coastal state in northwestern Germany. It is the second-largest state by land area, with 47,614 km2, and fourth-largest in population among the 16 Länder of the Federal Republic of Germany.

items.name: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern
items.blurb: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, often known by its anglicised name Mecklenburg–West Pomerania, is a coastal state in the north-east of Germany.

items.name: North Rhine-Westphalia
items.blurb: North Rhine-Westphalia or North-Rhine/Westphalia, commonly shortened to NRW, is a landlocked state in Western Germany. With more than 18 million inhabitants, it is the most populous state in Germany.

items.name: Rhineland-Palatinate
items.blurb: Rhineland-Palatinate is a landlocked state in western Germany. It covers 19,846 km2 and has about 4.05 million residents. It is the ninth largest and sixth most populous of the sixteen states.

items.name: Saarland
items.blurb: Saarland is a landlocked federal state of Germany in the southwest of the country. With an area of 2,570 km2 and a population of 1 million in 2024, it is the smallest German state in area apart from the city-states of Berlin, Bremen, and Hamburg, and the smallest in population apart from Bremen.

items.name: Saxony
items.blurb: Saxony, officially the Free State of Saxony, is a landlocked state of Germany, bordering the states of Brandenburg, Saxony-Anhalt, Thuringia, and Bavaria, as well as the countries of the Czechia and Poland.

items.name: Saxony-Anhalt
items.blurb: Saxony-Anhalt is a landlocked state of Germany. It covers an area of 20,555 square kilometres and has a population of about 2.14 million inhabitants, making it the 8th-largest state in Germany by area and the 11th-largest by population.

items.name: Schleswig-Holstein
items.blurb: Schleswig-Holstein is a coastal state that is the northernmost of the sixteen states of Germany, comprising most of the historical Duchy of Holstein and the southern part of the former Duchy of Schleswig.

items.name: Thuringia
items.blurb: Thuringia is a landlocked state in central Germany. With 2.1 million people, it is 12th-largest by population, and with 16,171 square kilometers, it is 11th-largest in area.
